dedupe_keys.name: iumenta framework for animal digital twins within the open digital twin platform odtp

description: IUMENTA, Latin for livestock, is a software framework for building and simulating digital twins of animals on the Open Digital Twin Platform, combining software sensors with data from different experiments to model animals' behavioural and physiological responses. The paper applies it to a digital twin of an animal's energy balance, updated in real time by the EnergyTag wearable software sensor, which tracks energy expenditure so that metabolic rates, nutritional needs and well-being can be estimated and the twin personalised. It was developed by Ali Youssef, Kristina Vodorezova, Yannick Aarts, Wisdom Agbeti, Arjan Palstra, Edwin Foekema, Leonel Aguilar, Ricardo da Silva Torres and Jascha Grübel and posted on arXiv on 4 November 2024 as a nine-page paper submitted to PerCom 2025. It is generic in location and species. The preprint is available free online as a PDF; the abstract page does not say where the software is published or under which licence, so it is not marked open source here. Caveats: it is a framework paper with one application, and the page read gives no validation results. For simulation it shows how livestock can be represented as digital twins driven by sensor data, useful for farm operations and for studying animal welfare during heat waves or feed supply disruptions. It is related to the Eclipse Ditto record in this catalogue, a general digital twin framework.
